EEBO-TCP is a partnership between the Universities of Michigan and Oxford and the publisher ProQuest to create accurately transcribed and encoded texts based on the image sets published by ProQuest via their Early English Books Online (EEBO) database (http://eebo.chadwyck.com). The general aim of EEBO-TCP is to encode one copy (usually the first edition) of every monographic English-language title published between 1473 and 1700 available in EEBO. EEBO-TCP aimed to produce large quantities of textual data within the usual project restraints of time and funding, and therefore chose to create diplomatic transcriptions (as opposed to critical editions) with light-touch, mainly structural encoding based on the Text Encoding Initiative (http://www.tei-c.org). The EEBO-TCP project was divided into two phases. The 25,363 texts created during Phase 1 of the project have been released into the public domain as of 1 January 2015. Anyone can now take and use these texts for their own purposes, but we respectfully request that due credit and attribution is given to their original source. Users should be aware of the process of creating the TCP texts, and therefore of any assumptions that can be made about the data. Text selection was based on the New Cambridge Bibliography of English Literature (NCBEL). If an author (or for an anonymous work, the title) appears in NCBEL, then their works are eligible for inclusion. Selection was intended to range over a wide variety of subject areas, to reflect the true nature of the print record of the period. In general, first editions of a works in English were prioritized, although there are a number of works in other languages, notably Latin and Welsh, included and sometimes a second or later edition of a work was chosen if there was a compelling reason to do so. sections.incipit: Whilest the gouernors in this  sort debated the matter with them, a certaine wicked and seditious person called Siba, the sonne of Bochri of the tribe of Beniamin, standing vp in the midst of the people began to crie out

sections.tail: nne of Bochri of the tribe of Beniamin, standing vp in the midst of the people began to crie out with a loud voyce, and to exclaime after this manner. We haue no part with Dauid, nor inheritance with the sonne of Iesse.

sections.incipit: This said, he sounded a trumpet, and proclaimed warre against the king; so that all men followed him, and forsooke Dauid. Onely the tribe of Iuda remained with him, and established him in the royall throne in Ierusalem:
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Sheba calls rebellion and Judah remains loyal at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: of Iuda remained with him, and established him in the royall throne in Ierusalem: where remouing his concubines (which  his son Absalon had knowen) out of his pallace, he neuer after that time had any company with them.

sections.incipit: After this he declared Amasa generall of the armie, and placed him in the same degree which Ioab had, neere vnto the person of the King: commanding him that he should assemble the greatest forces that he might out of the
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Amasa appointed and charged to gather Judah at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: e might out of the tribe of Iuda, & that within three daies he should return vnto him, to the end that hauing deliuered him both the armie & the place of generall, he might send him to make warre vpon the son of Bochri.

sections.incipit:
After that Amasa was departed, and employed his time in gathering vp his army; the king seeing that he failed to returne vpon the third day, told  
                        Ioab that it was not good to permit Siba to gath
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Amasa delays and David fears Sheba strength at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail:
he failed to returne vpon the third day, told  
                        Ioab that it was not good to permit Siba to gather a greater head by delay, & thereby breede vs more trouble and molestation then Absalon had done.

sections.incipit: For which cause (said he) stay thou not but take vnto thee those forces which thou hast in a readines, and my sixe hundreth men with thy  brother Abisai, and pursue thou the enemie, and in what place soeuer thou meetest
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of David orders immediate pursuit at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: r thou meetest him, by all meanes indeuour thy selfe to giue him the battell. Hast thee therefore, and ouertake him, for feare least he seaze some of our strongest Cities, and thereby procure vs much trauell and labour.

sections.incipit: Ioab with all expedition obeyed his commaundement, and tooke with him the aforesaid sixe hundreth, with his brother Abisai, and commaunded all the forces that were in Ierusalem to follow after him, and in this array issu
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Joab marches and meets Amasa at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: Siba. Now when he came vnto Gabaon (a burrow some fortie furlongs distant from Ierusalem) Amasa came & met with him, & brought with him great forces. Ioab hauing his sword girt by his side, and his curets on his backe,

sections.incipit: whilest Amasa came onward to salute him, subtilly and of set purpose let his sword slip out of his sheath, and taking it vp from the ground with one hand he drew neere vnto Amasa, vnder pretence
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Joab covertly kills Amasa at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: e had conceiued against a good young man & his cousen, who had in no sort offended him, and onely by reason of the estate of generall, which the king had giuen him; and because Dauid had equalled him in honour with him,

sections.incipit: for which very cause before that he had slaine. Abner. Notwithstanding this act of his seemed in some sort pardonable, by reason of the pretext which he pretended of the wrong done vnto his brother Azael, yet was not thi
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of comparison with earlier killing of Abner at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: Notwithstanding this act of his seemed in some sort pardonable, by reason of the pretext which he pretended of the wrong done vnto his brother Azael, yet was not this a sufficient colour to excuse the murther of Amasa.

sections.incipit: When this was done, he pursued Siba, and left a certaine man to wait vpon the bodie of Amasa, who had commaundement giuen him to proclaime with a loud voice thorow the whole armie, that he was iustly and deseruedly slain
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Joab pursues Sheba and leaves a proclamation at the corpse at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: iuen him to proclaime with a loud voice thorow the whole armie, that he was iustly and deseruedly slaine, commaunding  those that bare any fauour to the kings title, to follow their generall Ioab and his brother Abisai.

sections.incipit: Now whilest his body lay thus in the way, & al the multitude (as it is vsual in such like accidēts) flocked round about it, he that had the charge of the bodie took it vp, & bare it into a certain place farre out of the
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of corpse removed so army may proceed at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: in such like accidēts) flocked round about it, he that had the charge of the bodie took it vp, & bare it into a certain place farre out of the way, & couered it with a garment: which done, all the people followed Ioab.

sections.incipit:
Now whilest he pursued Siba thorow all the region of the Israelites, a certaine man told him that he had retired himself into a certaine strong citie called Abelmacha; where he no sooner arriued,

but that he begirt the
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Sheba located in a strong city and besieged at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail:
that he begirt the Citie, and entrenched it round about; commanding his souldiers to vndermine  
                         and ouerthrow the walles: for he was sore displeased because they had shut the gates against him.

sections.incipit: But a certaine honest and prudent woman, seeing her countrey in extreme perill, ascended the walles and called Ioab and his souldiers to a parlee, who comming forth to conferre with him, she spake after this manner: God
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of wise woman appeals to Joab at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: d they might destroy the enemies of the Hebrewes, and plant amongst them an vniuersall and perpetuall peace; but you inforce your selues to destroy one of the mother Cities of Israell, that hath in no sort offended you.

sections.incipit: Ioab praied God to be fauourable vnto them, and said that for his owne part it was not his meaning that any one of the Citie should die, neither his pretence to race and deface so famous a Citie; his intent was only, tha
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Joab seeks Sheba alone and promises withdrawal at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: ce so famous a Citie; his intent was only, that if Siba the sonne of Bochri, and the kings aduersarie were deliuered into his hands to doe iustice on him, to leuy the siege, and to  cause his army to retire from thence.

sections.incipit: When the woman had heard what Ioab had said, she praied him to stay a little while, promising him incontinently to cast his head ouer vnto him. Wherupon she came downe amongst the assembly of the Citizens, to whom she sp
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of woman asks brief delay and persuades citizens at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: e for a wicked mans cause, and a stranger whom ye know not? will you admit him in place of Dauid your king, from whose hands you haue receiued so many benefits? thinke you that one only Citie can resist so huge an army?

sections.incipit: After this manner perswaded she them to cut off Sibas head,  and to cast it into Ioabs campe: which done, Ioab commanded the retreat to be sounded, and leuied the siege, and returning backe into Ierusalem, was once more
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Sheba beheaded and Joab restores his command at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: to cut off Sibas head,  and to cast it into Ioabs campe: which done, Ioab commanded the retreat to be sounded, and leuied the siege, and returning backe into Ierusalem, was once more declared generall of all the people.

sections.incipit:
The king also appointed Banaia captaine of his guards, and of six hundreth souldiers.  
                        Adoram was made treasurer to gather in the tributes. Sabath and Achilaus had the charge of remembrancers.
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of royal officers after the rebellion at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail:
Adoram was made treasurer to gather in the tributes. Sabath and Achilaus had the charge of remembrancers.  
                        Susa was made secretarie. Sadoc and Abiathar were made the high priests.

sections.incipit: After this it hapned that the conntrey was afflicted with a famine: For which cause Dauid besought God that he would haue compassion on his people, and that it might please him to manifest not  onely the cause, but also
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of famine and Gibeonite grievance at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: answered him, that God  would be reuenged of the wrong done vnto the Gabeonites, whom king Saul had deceiued and traiterously slaine, without respect of the oath, which the gouernor Iosuah and the elders made vnto them.

sections.incipit: If therefore he would suffer the Gabeonites to reuenge the death of their slaughtered friends according to their desire, God had promised to be appeased, and to deliuer the people from their imminent & presenteuils.
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of divine requirement of reparation at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: If therefore he would suffer the Gabeonites to reuenge the death of their slaughtered friends according to their desire, God had promised to be appeased, and to deliuer the people from their imminent & presenteuils.

sections.incipit: As soone as he vnderstood by the prophets what God required,  he sent for the Gabeonites, and asked them what it was which they required: who wished him to deliuer into their hands seuen of Sauls sonnes to take their reu
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Gibeonites request seven sons and David complies at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: h they required: who wished him to deliuer into their hands seuen of Sauls sonnes to take their reuenge on them: whereupon the king made search after them, onely sparing and protecting Mephiboseth the sonne of Ionathan.

sections.incipit: When the Gabeonites had laid hold on these seuen, they executed them according to  their pleasures: and thereupon God incontinently sent downe raine and disposed the earth to beare fruit; moistning and alaying the drouth
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of execution and restored rainfall at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: easures: and thereupon God incontinently sent downe raine and disposed the earth to beare fruit; moistning and alaying the drouth forepassed, so that the land of the Hebrewes recouered againe his pristine fruitfulnesse.

sections.incipit: Not long after the king made warre vpon the Philistines, and at such time as the battell was striken, and the enemies turned their backes, it chanced that the king hotly pursuing the chase was left alone; and discouered
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of David pursues the defeated enemy alone at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: as the battell was striken, and the enemies turned their backes, it chanced that the king hotly pursuing the chase was left alone; and discouered in his wearinesse by one of the enemies called Acmon, the sonne of Araph

sections.incipit: of the race of the Giants, who beside his sword  had a iauelin, the point whereof waied three hundreth sicles, and a corselet tissued with chaines,  who returning backe charged Dauid very violently, with an intent to kil
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of giant weapons and Abishai rescue at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: tent to kill the king of his enemies, by reason that he saw him spent with trauell. But about the same instant Abisai Ioabs brother arriued in the place, who stept betweene them and rescued the king, and slew his enemy.

sections.incipit: The whole army for a little space were grieuously discomforted, in regard of the danger wherein  the king had been, and the gouernors swore that he should neuer afterwards enter into battel with them, for feare least he
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of army requires David cease personal combat at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: by that meanes should depriue the people of those gifts which were in him, which he had already made them feele, and whereof hereafter they should be made partakers, if God should vouchsafe him a long and blessed life.

sections.incipit:
The king hauing intelligence that the Philistines were assembled  
                         in the citie of Gazara, sent out an army against them, in which Sabach the Hittite, one of Dauids redoubted and picked souldiers
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Sibbechai victory at Gazara at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: or he slew diuers of them that vaunted themselues to be of the race of the Giants, and that were verie proud and puffed vp with presumption of their valour, and was chiefe authour of that victorie which the Hebrewes had.

sections.incipit:
After this last receiued losse, the Philistines once more hazarded their fortunes in warre, against

whō when Dauid had sent out an army, Nephanus his kinsman shewed himself very valiant:  
                         For
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of renewed war and Nephan single combat at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: For fighting hand to hand against him that was accounted the most valiant champion amongst all the Philistines, he slew him, and put the rest to flight; of whom verie many died in that battell also,

sections.incipit: In processe of time they reincamped neere vnto a Citie not farre from the frontiers of the countrey of the Hebrewes: In which army of theirs there was a man six cubits hie, who had on either foote and either hand, a fing
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of another campaign and six-fingered giant at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: rre from the frontiers of the countrey of the Hebrewes: In which army of theirs there was a man six cubits hie, who had on either foote and either hand, a finger more then the accustomed bequest of nature affoorded him.

sections.incipit: Against him Ionathan the son of Sama (one of those that were sent by Dauid in this army) fought  hand to hand & slew him: so that approuing himselfe to be the meanes of that victorie, he bare away the honor of the battel
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Jonathan defeats the giant and ends hostilities at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: ictorie, he bare away the honor of the battell, and praise of his valour: for this Philistine boasted likewise that he was descended from the race of the Giants. After this battell they warred no more on the Israelites.

sections.incipit: Hereupon Dauid deliuered from war and danger, and euer after enioying a perfect peace,  composed Odes and hymnes in praise of God, in diuers kindes of verse: for some are of three, other  some are of fiue measures. He ma
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of David hymns and musical instruments at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: ymnes in praise of God, in diuers kindes of verse: for some are of three, other  some are of fiue measures. He made instruments also, and taught the Leuites to praise God vpon them, on the Saboth daies and other feasts.

sections.incipit: The forme of these instruments was after this manner. The Cinnare is composed of ten strings, and is plaid vpon with a bow. The Nable containeth twelue sounds or cords, and is striken with the fingers. The Cimbals were l
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of instrument construction described at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: ds or cords, and is striken with the fingers. The Cimbals were large and great and made of brasse, of which it sufficeth in this sort to make some mention, least the nature of those instruments should wholy be vnknowne.

sections.incipit: Now all those that were about the king were valiant men: but amongst all the rest, there were eight most notable and heroick men. The noble  actions of fiue of which I will declare, because they might suffice to exemplif
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of introduction to the celebrated warriors at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: The noble  actions of fiue of which I will declare, because they might suffice to exemplifie the vertues that were in the other that remained: for they were capable to gouerne a countrey, and to conquer  diuers nations.

sections.incipit: The first of them was Issemus the sonne of Achemaeus, who hauing verie oftentimes  thrust himselfe into the midst of his disordered enemies, neuer gaue ouer fighting till he had slain nine hundreth of them. After him was
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of first warrior and introduction to Eleazar at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: tentimes  thrust himselfe into the midst of his disordered enemies, neuer gaue ouer fighting till he had slain nine hundreth of them. After him was Eleazar the sonne of Dodeias, who had accompanied the  king in Sarphat.

sections.incipit: He in a certaine battell (wherein thorow the huge multitude of the enemies, the Israelites were affrighted and put to flight) onely kept his place and affronted the enemy, and rushing in amongst them made a great slaught
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Eleazar stands alone and defeats the Philistines at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: t to flight by him, came downe and ranne vpon them, and obtained a miraculous and famous victorie ouer them. For Eleazar slaughtered those that fled, and the rest of the army followed and spoyled those that were slaine.

sections.incipit:
The third was the sonne of Ilus called Sebas, who fighting against  
                         the Philistines, in a place called the Iawe (and seeing the Hebrewes to be affraid of their power, and almost out of heart) re
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of third warrior stands alone at Lehi at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: their power, and almost out of heart) resisted them alone, as if he had bin an arraunged army, and slew some of them, and pursued and put the rest to flight, in that they were vnable to sustaine his force and violence.

sections.incipit: These three exploited with their owne hands these executions of warre. About that time that the king liued in Ierusalem, the army of the Philistines came out to make warre vpon him, and Dauid (as we haue declared heretof
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of three warriors and Bethlehem water episode at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: d in Ierusalem, the army of the Philistines came out to make warre vpon him, and Dauid (as we haue declared heretofore) was gone vp into the higher citie to aske counsell of God, what the euent of that warre should bee,

sections.incipit: and the enemies being incamped in that valley (that extendeth it selfe as farre as Bethleem, a Citie some twentie furlongs distant from Ierusalem) Dauid said to his companions: There is verie good water in the place wher
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of enemy deployment and David desire for water at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail:
e I was born, and especially that which is in the pitte which is neere vnto the gate, if any one will bring me of  
                         that water to drinke, I shall esteeme it more then if he gaue me great riches.

sections.incipit: These three men hearing these words, instantly ranne out, and past thorow the enemies campe, and went to Bethleem, where hauing drawne water, they returned backe vnto the king, sallying thorow the midst of their enemies,
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of warriors obtain water through the enemy camp at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: orow the midst of their enemies, bringing newes that the Philistines being affraid of their hardinesse, and great courage, kept themselues vpon their guard, not daring to charge them; notwithstanding their small number.

sections.incipit: But the king tasted not of this water which they brought him, saying that it was bought with the danger of mens liues, and therefore that it was no reason he should drinke thereof, but he powred it out as an oblation vnt
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of David dedicates rather than drinks the water at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: ues, and therefore that it was no reason he should drinke thereof, but he powred it out as an oblation vnto God, giuing him thankes because he had deliuered his seruants. After these three followed Abisai Ioabs brother,

sections.incipit: who slew six hundreth of the enemy  in one day. The fift was Banaia of the race of the Leuites, who being defied by certaine  brothers, famous amongst the Moabites for their vertue, ouercame them. Moreouer, a certaine  A
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Abishai feat and Benaiah victories at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: ue, ouercame them. Moreouer, a certaine  Aegyptian of a wonderfull stature, hauing defied him (notwithstanding the said Banaia was naked and the other armed) yet charged he him, and tooke away his iauelin and slewe him.

sections.incipit: To  these foresaid actes of his, a man may annex this as the most valiant, or very neerely equalling the rest. For it came to passe, that after a certaine snow a Lyon tossing amidst the flakes thereof, fell into a pit (w
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Benaiah further exploit with a lion introduced at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail:
o narrow, that a man could not discerne where it was, especially

for that at the same time it was couered with snow) where being inclosed, and seeing no means  
                         to escape, he roared out amaine:

sections.incipit: which when Banaia who passed that way heard, he followed the voice, and drew neere vnto the place; and afterwards went downe into the pit, where with a staffe he bare in his hand he fought with, ouercame, and slew the Ly
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Benaiah descends and kills the lion at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: voice, and drew neere vnto the place; and afterwards went downe into the pit, where with a staffe he bare in his hand he fought with, ouercame, and slew the Lyon. The thirtie three other were of like valour and vertue.

sections.incipit: But King Dauid being desirous to know how many thousands of men he could number amongst the people, and forgetting the commaundement ordained by Moses (who had giuen order that if the people had beene numbred, there shou
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of David orders census forgetting Mosaic requirement at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: d forgetting the commaundement ordained by Moses (who had giuen order that if the people had beene numbred, there should be paid vnto God for euerie head halfe a sicle) he commanded Ioab to go and number all the people:

sections.incipit: and although Ioab had manifestly proued vnto him that it was a thing no waies necessarie; yet could he not perswade him, but that he enioyned him with all expedition, to set forward on his way, and muster the people of t
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of Joab protests and conducts the census at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: of the Hebrewes, to know how many men there were, and at the end of nine moneths and twenty daies, he returned to Ierusalem to the king, and presented him with the list of the people, the tribe of Beniamin only excepted

sections.incipit: (for he neither numbred that tribe, nor the tribe of Leui.) This done, the king perceiuing that he had displeased God, was verie sorrowful and pensiue.  The route of the other Israelites was of nine hundreth thousand men
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of excluded tribes remorse and census total at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: God, was verie sorrowful and pensiue.  The route of the other Israelites was of nine hundreth thousand men, able to beare armes, and to follow the warre, besides that the only tribe of Iuda contained 400. thousand men.

sections.incipit: When the Prophets had certified Dauid how God was displeased with him, he began to pray & beseech him that it might please him to appease his wrath, and to pardon his offence. Hereupon God sent the Prophet Gad vnto him,
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of anger of God and three offered punishments at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: hould raigne in his countries; or that warre for three moneths space should afflict the same, wherein he should haue the worst; or that the plague and pestilence should for three daies space raunge amongst the Hebrewes.

sections.incipit: Being thus distraught and troubled by reason of his difficult election, amidst these imminent miseries; and the Prophet vrging him to returne a short answere, whereby God might be satisfied: the king bethinking him that
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of David considers the choice and unequal famine risk at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: hould aske famine, he should rather seeme to respect his owne securitie, then the common-weale, in that no daunger might by that meanes touch him, for that he had great store of corne in his barne, and they vnfurnished;

sections.incipit: and if for three moneths he should make choise to be ouercome by the enemy, in that case also he might seeme to haue care of himselfe, in that he had many strong Castles and a valiant guard of men to attend
sections.rationale: Earliest surviving Lodge counterpart of David rejects military punishment and chooses plague at the Greek/Latin Niese opening. Whiston is additional correspondence evidence. Native wording and order retained.
sections.tail: plague, that was both as incident to the prince, as the subiect; wherein each man was touched with equall and imminent feare, saying, that it was better to fall into the hands of God, then into the hands of his enemies.

sections.incipit: When the Prophet had receiued this answere from him, he reported it vnto God; who sent a plague and mortalitie amongst the Hebrewes, whereby they died after diuers manners: so that it was very hard to discerne the malady
